input_references.role: Timestamped points with matched-road coordinates, speed, context, and event attributes

metadata.goal: Investigate changes in travel behavior and movement conditions under varying environmental conditions.
metadata.category: Distance-conditioned weather speed gaps, turn reductions, and spatial extent
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed WorldTrace case with 700 trajectories. Geometry source: Observed map-matched NYC WorldTrace road paths or continuous road-aligned return traversals. Environmental, temporal, mode, vehicle, and event attributes are arranged to make all stated comparisons measurable without changing the route coordinates used by the figures.

insight_list.question: Does the rainy-versus-dry car-speed difference become larger on longer routes?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the same source-route families in rainy and dry weather, then relate each route family's speed gap to its distance.
insight_list.code:
c=df[df.travel_mode.eq('car')].copy()
route=(c.groupby(['source_trajectory_id','weather']).agg(distance_km=('trajectory_distance_km','mean'),speed_kmh=('mean_speed_kmh','mean')).reset_index())
pivot=route.pivot(index='source_trajectory_id',columns='weather',values='speed_kmh');pivot['distance_km']=route.groupby('source_trajectory_id').distance_km.mean();pivot['dry_minus_rainy_kmh']=pivot.sunny-pivot.rainy;pivot=pivot.sort_values('distance_km')
print('Overall car speed by weather');print(c.groupby('weather').mean_speed_kmh.agg(['mean','std','count']).round(2));print('Matched-route speed gaps');print(pivot.round(2));print('distance-gap correlation',round(pivot.distance_km.corr(pivot.dry_minus_rainy_kmh),3))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(1,2,figsize=(12,4.8),constrained_layout=True)
for weather,color in [('rainy','#2563eb'),('sunny','#f59e0b')]:
    q=route[route.weather.eq(weather)].sort_values('distance_km');ax[0].plot(q.distance_km,q.speed_kmh,marker='o',linewidth=2,label=weather,color=color)
ax[0].set(title='Car speed by route length and weather',xlabel='trajectory distance (km)',ylabel='mean speed (km/h)');ax[0].legend();ax[0].grid(alpha=.25)
ax[1].plot(pivot.distance_km,pivot.dry_minus_rainy_kmh,marker='o',linewidth=2,color='#dc2626');ax[1].set(title='Rain penalty grows on longer car trips',xlabel='trajectory distance (km)',ylabel='dry minus rainy speed (km/h)');ax[1].grid(alpha=.25)
plt.show()

insight_list.question: How does the local speed reduction at frequent turns vary between rainy and mild weather across temperatures?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Derive each trajectory's ordinary-section minus high-turn-section speed from point observations, then aggregate by weather and temperature.
insight_list.code:
q=user_df[user_df.travel_mode.eq('car')].copy()
per_trip=q.groupby(['trajectory_id','weather','temperature_c','is_high_turn_segment']).speed_kmh.mean().unstack('is_high_turn_segment');per_trip['observed_reduction_kmh']=per_trip[False]-per_trip[True]
g=per_trip.groupby(['weather','temperature_c']).observed_reduction_kmh.agg(['mean','std','count']);print(g.round(2))
fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8,5),constrained_layout=True)
for weather,color in [('rainy','#2563eb'),('sunny','#f59e0b')]:
    z=g.xs(weather,level='weather');ax.errorbar(z.index,z['mean'],yerr=z['std'],marker='o',capsize=3,linewidth=2,label=weather,color=color)
ax.set(title='Local speed reduction at frequent turns',xlabel='temperature (°C)',ylabel='ordinary minus high-turn speed (km/h)');ax.legend(title='weather');ax.grid(alpha=.25);plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Although car travel becomes more dominant during poor weather, the car trajectories in such cases are concentrated in relatively shorter-distance movements and do not increase the overall spatial extent of mobility.

insight_list.question: Does poor-weather car dominance expand mobility, or is it concentrated in shorter trajectories?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare mode shares and car-distance distributions, then directly compare the aggregate geographic footprints covered by all poor- and mild-weather car trajectories.

insights: Rainy trajectories exhibit lower average speeds than dry-weather trajectories, but the reduction is substantially stronger for longer car trips than for short car trips.
During adverse weather, trajectories with frequent turns experience larger local speed reductions compared to trajectories in mild weather conditions.

Although car travel becomes more dominant during poor weather, the car trajectories in such cases are concentrated in relatively shorter-distance movements and do not increase the overall spatial extent of mobility.
summary: Rainy trajectories exhibit lower average speeds than dry-weather trajectories, but the reduction is substantially stronger for longer car trips than for short car trips. During adverse weather, trajectories with frequent turns experience larger local speed reductions compared to trajectories in mild weather conditions. Although car travel becomes more dominant during poor weather, the car trajectories in such cases are concentrated in relatively shorter-distance movements and do not increase the overall spatial extent of mobility.
